So the compiler veto ran against my proposed content in memory, and the only feedback was "fault_covered not discharged". I can't verify paths on a file that doesn't exist (the protocol even says: if the target does not exist, draft it and don't verify).

Also note the rule list for v1 spec set: deterministic, read_only, retry_safe, idempotent, state_isolated, fault_covered, no_secret_leakage, no_credential_leakage, input_validated, pii_contained, injection_safe. Hmm — canonical and cost_bounded are NOT in that v1 spec set list! So maybe `canonical` and `cost_bounded` aren't valid Proof spec names... but wait, the meta example validated-fetch-query used a union including "canonical" and "cost_bounded" — that was from the example registry, which may be aspirational/larger. The spec set from this rule says use one of: deterministic, read_only, retry_safe, idempotent, state_isolated, fault_covered, no_secret_leakage, no_credential_leakage, input_validated, pii_contained, injection_safe.

If canonical/cost_bounded were invalid names, I'd get ZTS502 spec_unknown_name, not fault_covered failure. So they're accepted (maybe recognized but the rule list is abbreviated, or maybe the proof engine treats them specially). Anyway, the failing spec is fault_covered, so focus there.

Since the file doesn't exist on disk, I need to reason about fault_covered from the rule semantics. Let me query describe_rule for "fault_covered" specifically — the search_rules query returned the spec_unknown_name rule because "fault_covered" appears in its help text. Let me instead describe_rule("fault_covered") directly to get its semantics, and maybe check what effects the fetch module introduces — but the file isn't on disk, so effects won't work.

Actually, better tool: zts_expert_review_patch with my content — it simulates an edit and reports new vs preexisting violations, possibly with more detail than the veto. Let me try that. It takes file + content. Since the file doesn't exist, before must be... I can pass just content. Let me try.

Also I could use zts_expert_prove_patch — but that needs before/after.

Let me use zts_expert_review_patch(file: "handler.ts", content: <my draft>) to see the full diagnostics. That might reveal which fault is uncovered.

Also describe_rule("fault_covered") for semantics. Two calls, one batch.","tool_calls":[{"index":0,"id":"call_00_OwNyIqSPxizsElYBrXFc3335","type":"function","function":{"name":"zts_expert_review_patch","arguments":"{"file": "handler.ts", "content": "import { fetch } from \"zttp:fetch\";\n\nexport function handler(req: Request): Proof<Response,\n  | \"deterministic\"\n  | \"state_isolated\"\n  | \"fault_covered\"\n  | \"result_safe\"\n  | \"optional_safe\"\n  | \"no_secret_leakage\"\n  | \"no_credential_leakage\"\n  | \"input_validated\"\n  | \"pii_contained\"\n  | \"injection_safe\"\n  | \"canonical\"\n  | \"cost_bounded\"\n> {\n  const upstream = fetch(\"https://api.example.com/v1/status\", {\n    method: \"GET\",\n    headers: { accept: \"application/json\" },\n    maxResponseBytes: 65536,\n  });\n  if (!upstream.ok) {\n    return Response.json({ error: \"upstream request failed\" }, { status: 502 });\n  }\n  return Response.json(upstream.json());\n}\n"}"}},{"index":1,"id":"call_01_npS2rMZsZvBj37MIwMTi0872","type":"function","function":{"name":"zts_expert_query","arguments":"{"operation": "describe_rule", "rule": "fault_covered"}"}}]},"logprobs":null,"finish_reason":"tool_calls"}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":11247,"completion_tokens":971,"total_tokens":12218,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":9344},"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":603},"prompt_cache_hit_tokens":9344,"prompt_cache_miss_tokens":1903},"system_fingerprint":"a26a7955944dc5c60445bff77fac9c8e"}
